{
  "plan": "# Formulário do Rodapé Unificado + Integração RD Station\n\n> **Status:** pronto para revisão — Parte 1 validada com user (abordagem A); Parte 2 consolidada com base nos relatórios de 3 agentes paralelos sobre a API RD Station.\n\n## Contexto\n\nHoje o footer do site `concertacao.bureau-it.com` (Concertação Pela Amazônia) renderiza **dois widgets Form do Elementor Pro completamente separados** no template footer ID 72234:\n\n- **Container `d1e32f6` (desktop/tablet)** — \"Cadastre-se para receber novidades\", layout horizontal compacto, inputs retangulares com borda branca sobre fundo verde, botão à direita. `custom_id` do select: `form_regiao`, label \"regiao\".\n- **Container `3e45cefe` (mobile)** — \"Inscreva-se para fazer parte da rede e saber mais sobre nossas iniciativas e eventos:\", layout vertical, inputs pill brancos arredondados (border-radius alto), botão centralizado abaixo. `custom_id` do select: `form_email_regiao`, label \"estado\".\n\nA divergência de `custom_id` entre as duas instâncias é um **bug funcional** silencioso: submissões coletadas via Newsletter caem em colunas diferentes dependendo se a pessoa preencheu no desktop ou no mobile. Além disso, o select de Região tem `\"Região\"` como uma `<option>` real (não usa `field_options_empty` do Elementor Pro), então um usuário que clica \"ENVIAR\" sem trocar o select envia o termo literal `\"Região\"` como se fosse a UF escolhida.\n\nO objetivo é eliminar a duplicação:\n\n1. **Um único widget Form** capaz de renderizar os dois designs distintos via controles responsivos device-aware (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile) — mantendo todas as integrações nativas do Elementor Pro Forms (webhook, MailChimp, ActiveCampaign etc.).\n2. **Corrigir o placeholder de Região** para que `\"Região\"` apareça como prompt do select (`<option value=\"\" disabled selected>`) e não seja enviado como dado.\n3. **Adicionar uma Form Action customizada** que envie os submits diretamente para o RD Station Marketing via API Key REST (`POST /platform/conversions`), sem depender de plugin third-party. Detalhamento da escolha API Key vs OAuth na Parte 2.\n\nA solução deve seguir o padrão BIT do projeto: mu-plugin em `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/` + cópia canônica em `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` do server-tools, commitado.\n\n---\n\n## Parte 1 — Mu-plugin `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php`\n\n### Abordagem aprovada (Abordagem A)\n\nEstender o widget Form **nativo** do Elementor Pro via hooks (não criar widget novo). Tornar device-aware (`responsive => true`) os controles que hoje não são, e adicionar 1 controle novo:\n\n| Controle | Nível no painel | Tipo | Por que |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `form_name` (já existe) | Form widget — Form Fields section | text → **torna-se responsive** | \"Cadastre-se...\" vs \"Inscreva-se...\" |\n| `placeholder` (já existe) | Repeater field — qualquer tipo | text → **torna-se responsive** | \"E-mail\" vs \"Insira seu melhor email\" |\n| `field_options_empty` (já existe no Pro p/ select) | Repeater field — só `select` | text → **torna-se responsive** | Placeholder \"Região\" do select |\n\nA UX no painel usa o **switcher device-aware nativo do Elementor** (ícone 🖥/📱 no topo do painel) — convenção que o editor já conhece de padding/font-size/margin.\n\n### Arquivos\n\n- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` (~150 linhas PHP)\n- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.css` (~80 linhas CSS — consolidar custom CSS inline atual + cobrir os 8 deltas)\n- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.js` (~30 linhas JS — micro-listener `matchMedia` para trocar atributo `placeholder` no resize)\n- Cópia canônica para `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` (3 arquivos).\n\n### Hooks PHP principais\n\n```php\n// 1. Tornar 'form_name' responsive no widget Form\nadd_action('elementor/element/form/section_form_fields/before_section_end', function ($element, $args) {\n    $element->update_control('form_name', ['responsive' => true]);\n}, 10, 2);\n\n// 2. Tornar 'placeholder' e 'field_options_empty' responsive nos fields (repeater)\nadd_action('elementor/element/form/section_form_fields/before_section_end', function ($element, $args) {\n    $form_fields = $element->get_controls('form_fields');\n    if (isset($form_fields['fields']['placeholder'])) {\n        $form_fields['fields']['placeholder']['responsive'] = true;\n    }\n    if (isset($form_fields['fields']['field_options_empty'])) {\n        $form_fields['fields']['field_options_empty']['responsive'] = true;\n    }\n    // update via set_settings — Elementor API exata será validada ao implementar\n}, 11, 2);\n\n// 3. Filter no render — injetar data-attrs com valores tablet/mobile\nadd_filter('elementor/widget/render_content', function ($content, $widget) {\n    if ($widget->get_name() !== 'form') return $content;\n    // parsear $widget->get_settings_for_display() — pegar form_name_tablet, form_name_mobile,\n    // placeholders por field por device — e injetar como data-bit-placeholder-{tablet,mobile}\n    return $content;\n}, 10, 2);\n```\n\n### Renderização do placeholder responsivo\n\nComo `placeholder` é atributo HTML (não estilo CSS), `@media` não consegue trocá-lo. Solução escolhida:\n\n- PHP renderiza o atributo `placeholder` com o valor **Desktop** + 2 data-attrs: `data-bit-placeholder-tablet` e `data-bit-placeholder-mobile`.\n- JS de ~30 linhas com `matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)')` e `matchMedia('(max-width: 1024px)')` troca o atributo `placeholder` no load e em resize/orientation change.\n- Mesma lógica para `<option>` do select (substitui texto da primeira `<option disabled selected>`).\n\nPerformance: enqueueado só nas páginas com widget Form (via `wp_enqueue_script` dentro do hook de render).\n\n### CSS — 8 deltas mapeados\n\nTodos cobertos por media queries dentro de `bit-elementor-form-responsive.css`:\n\n| # | Propriedade | Desktop | Mobile |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Heading text | (controle PHP) | (controle PHP) |\n| 2 | Placeholder email | (controle PHP) | (controle PHP) |\n| 3 | Layout fields | `flex-direction: row` | `flex-direction: column` |\n| 4 | Border-radius input | `4px` | `24px` (pill) |\n| 5 | Background input | `transparent` | `#fff` |\n| 6 | Cor placeholder | branco fade | verde menta fade |\n| 7 | Posição botão | inline final | centralizado em row própria |\n| 8 | Largura botão | flex (~20%) | compacto (~30%, centered) |\n\nCSS escopado em `.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive` — classe adicionada via filter `elementor/widget/render_content` somente quando o widget tem ID/classe esperada (evita afetar OUTROS forms do site).\n\n### Migração dos 2 widgets atuais → 1 widget\n\nScript de migração standalone `scripts/unify-footer-form.php` (idempotente, com `--dry-run`):\n\n1. Carregar `_elementor_data` do template footer ID 72234.\n2. Localizar containers `d1e32f6` e `3e45cefe`.\n3. Manter o widget Form do desktop (`d1e32f6`) como base — tem o `custom_id` correto (`form_regiao`).\n4. Para cada controle responsivo (form_name, placeholder, field_options_empty): copiar o valor do widget mobile para o sufixo `_mobile` do widget desktop.\n5. Remover o container mobile (`3e45cefe`).\n6. Remover a classe `hidden-mobile` / restrições `hide_*` do desktop.\n7. Validar com Playwright (gate visual desktop + mobile + tablet em `cambrasmax.local:8484`).\n\n### Backwards compat / paridade dev↔prod\n\n- Mu-plugin é DEV-ONLY até validar em dev; depois copiar para `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` e fazer deploy via phase3/share deploy para HML/PROD.\n- Antes do deploy prod do script de unificação: backup do template 72234 via `wp post get 72234 --field=content > backup-template-72234-pre-unify.txt`.\n\n---\n\n## Parte 2 — Integração RD Station (mu-plugin `bit-elementor-form-rdstation.php`)\n\n> Pesquisa consolidada de 3 agentes paralelos (relatórios completos em `/Users/dcambria/.claude/plans/image-5-image-6-magical-lightning-agent-{ae9a161c70e9caa22,a2f8a67c2b3b2de69,a1e49fbb675f2ed90}.md`).\n\n### Decisão de autenticação: API Key (não OAuth 2.0)\n\nA integração é **single-tenant** (uma conta RD do cliente, BIT controla o site). ## Approved Plan:
# Formulário do Rodapé Unificado + Integração RD Station

> **Status:** pronto para revisão — Parte 1 validada com user (abordagem A); Parte 2 consolidada com base nos relatórios de 3 agentes paralelos sobre a API RD Station.

## Contexto

Hoje o footer do site `concertacao.bureau-it.com` (Concertação Pela Amazônia) renderiza **dois widgets Form do Elementor Pro completamente separados** no template footer ID 72234:

- **Container `d1e32f6` (desktop/tablet)** — "Cadastre-se para receber novidades", layout horizontal compacto, inputs retangulares com borda branca sobre fundo verde, botão à direita. `custom_id` do select: `form_regiao`, label "regiao".
- **Container `3e45cefe` (mobile)** — "Inscreva-se para fazer parte da rede e saber mais sobre nossas iniciativas e eventos:", layout vertical, inputs pill brancos arredondados (border-radius alto), botão centralizado abaixo. `custom_id` do select: `form_email_regiao`, label "estado".

A divergência de `custom_id` entre as duas instâncias é um **bug funcional** silencioso: submissões coletadas via Newsletter caem em colunas diferentes dependendo se a pessoa preencheu no desktop ou no mobile. Além disso, o select de Região tem `"Região"` como uma `<option>` real (não usa `field_options_empty` do Elementor Pro), então um usuário que clica "ENVIAR" sem trocar o select envia o termo literal `"Região"` como se fosse a UF escolhida.

O objetivo é eliminar a duplicação:

1. **Um único widget Form** capaz de renderizar os dois designs distintos via controles responsivos device-aware (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile) — mantendo todas as integrações nativas do Elementor Pro Forms (webhook, MailChimp, ActiveCampaign etc.).
2. **Corrigir o placeholder de Região** para que `"Região"` apareça como prompt do select (`<option value="" disabled selected>`) e não seja enviado como dado.
3. **Adicionar uma Form Action customizada** que envie os submits diretamente para o RD Station Marketing via API Key REST (`POST /platform/conversions`), sem depender de plugin third-party. Detalhamento da escolha API Key vs OAuth na Parte 2.

A solução deve seguir o padrão BIT do projeto: mu-plugin em `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/` + cópia canônica em `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` do server-tools, commitado.

---

## Parte 1 — Mu-plugin `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php`

### Abordagem aprovada (Abordagem A)

Estender o widget Form **nativo** do Elementor Pro via hooks (não criar widget novo). Tornar device-aware (`responsive => true`) os controles que hoje não são, e adicionar 1 controle novo:

| Controle | Nível no painel | Tipo | Por que |
|---|---|---|---|
| `form_name` (já existe) | Form widget — Form Fields section | text → **torna-se responsive** | "Cadastre-se..." vs "Inscreva-se..." |
| `placeholder` (já existe) | Repeater field — qualquer tipo | text → **torna-se responsive** | "E-mail" vs "Insira seu melhor email" |
| `field_options_empty` (já existe no Pro p/ select) | Repeater field — só `select` | text → **torna-se responsive** | Placeholder "Região" do select |

A UX no painel usa o **switcher device-aware nativo do Elementor** (ícone 🖥/📱 no topo do painel) — convenção que o editor já conhece de padding/font-size/margin.

### Arquivos

- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` (~150 linhas PHP)
- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.css` (~80 linhas CSS — consolidar custom CSS inline atual + cobrir os 8 deltas)
- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.js` (~30 linhas JS — micro-listener `matchMedia` para trocar atributo `placeholder` no resize)
- Cópia canônica para `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` (3 arquivos).

### Hooks PHP principais

```php
// 1. Tornar 'form_name' responsive no widget Form
add_action('elementor/element/form/section_form_fields/before_section_end', function ($element, $args) {
    $element->update_control('form_name', ['responsive' => true]);
}, 10, 2);

// 2. Tornar 'placeholder' e 'field_options_empty' responsive nos fields (repeater)
add_action('elementor/element/form/section_form_fields/before_section_end', function ($element, $args) {
    $form_fields = $element->get_controls('form_fields');
    if (isset($form_fields['fields']['placeholder'])) {
        $form_fields['fields']['placeholder']['responsive'] = true;
    }
    if (isset($form_fields['fields']['field_options_empty'])) {
        $form_fields['fields']['field_options_empty']['responsive'] = true;
    }
    // update via set_settings — Elementor API exata será validada ao implementar
}, 11, 2);

// 3. Filter no render — injetar data-attrs com valores tablet/mobile
add_filter('elementor/widget/render_content', function ($content, $widget) {
    if ($widget->get_name() !== 'form') return $content;
    // parsear $widget->get_settings_for_display() — pegar form_name_tablet, form_name_mobile,
    // placeholders por field por device — e injetar como data-bit-placeholder-{tablet,mobile}
    return $content;
}, 10, 2);
```

### Renderização do placeholder responsivo

Como `placeholder` é atributo HTML (não estilo CSS), `@media` não consegue trocá-lo. Solução escolhida:

- PHP renderiza o atributo `placeholder` com o valor **Desktop** + 2 data-attrs: `data-bit-placeholder-tablet` e `data-bit-placeholder-mobile`.
- JS de ~30 linhas com `matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)')` e `matchMedia('(max-width: 1024px)')` troca o atributo `placeholder` no load e em resize/orientation change.
- Mesma lógica para `<option>` do select (substitui texto da primeira `<option disabled selected>`).

Performance: enqueueado só nas páginas com widget Form (via `wp_enqueue_script` dentro do hook de render).

### CSS — 8 deltas mapeados

Todos cobertos por media queries dentro de `bit-elementor-form-responsive.css`:

| # | Propriedade | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Heading text | (controle PHP) | (controle PHP) |
| 2 | Placeholder email | (controle PHP) | (controle PHP) |
| 3 | Layout fields | `flex-direction: row` | `flex-direction: column` |
| 4 | Border-radius input | `4px` | `24px` (pill) |
| 5 | Background input | `transparent` | `#fff` |
| 6 | Cor placeholder | branco fade | verde menta fade |
| 7 | Posição botão | inline final | centralizado em row própria |
| 8 | Largura botão | flex (~20%) | compacto (~30%, centered) |

CSS escopado em `.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive` — classe adicionada via filter `elementor/widget/render_content` somente quando o widget tem ID/classe esperada (evita afetar OUTROS forms do site).

### Migração dos 2 widgets atuais → 1 widget

Script de migração standalone `scripts/unify-footer-form.php` (idempotente, com `--dry-run`):

1. Carregar `_elementor_data` do template footer ID 72234.
2. Localizar containers `d1e32f6` e `3e45cefe`.
3. Manter o widget Form do desktop (`d1e32f6`) como base — tem o `custom_id` correto (`form_regiao`).
4. Para cada controle responsivo (form_name, placeholder, field_options_empty): copiar o valor do widget mobile para o sufixo `_mobile` do widget desktop.
5. Remover o container mobile (`3e45cefe`).
6. Remover a classe `hidden-mobile` / restrições `hide_*` do desktop.
7. Salvar `_elementor_data` com `wp_slash(wp_json_encode(...))` (lição: `[[feedback_elementor_data_wp_slash_required]]`).
8. `wp elementor flush-css && warm-up explícito do template 72234` (lição: `[[feedback_elementor_flush_css_warmup]]`).
9. Validar com Playwright (gate visual desktop + mobile + tablet em `cambrasmax.local:8484`).

### Backwards compat / paridade dev↔prod

- Mu-plugin é DEV-ONLY até validar em dev; depois copiar para `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/` e fazer deploy via phase3/share deploy para HML/PROD.
- Antes do deploy prod do script de unificação: backup do template 72234 via `wp post get 72234 --field=content > backup-template-72234-pre-unify.txt`.

## Parte 2 — Integração RD Station (mu-plugin `bit-elementor-form-rdstation.php`)

> Pesquisa consolidada de 3 agentes paralelos (relatórios completos em `/Users/dcambria/.claude/plans/image-5-image-6-magical-lightning-agent-{ae9a161c70e9caa22,a2f8a67c2b3b2de69,a1e49fbb675f2ed90}.md`).

### Decisão de autenticação: API Key (não OAuth 2.0)

A integração é **single-tenant** (uma conta RD do cliente, BIT controla o site). API Key elimina toda a complexidade de OAuth — sem refresh token, sem cron, sem encryption-at-rest, sem callback de autorização. Trade-off aceitável: API Key tem limite de 5/conta, mas só usamos 1. OAuth ficaria sobre-engineered para o caso.

**Credenciais já provisionadas pelo user:**

Os tokens estão hoje em `docker-dev/sites/concertacao/.env`:

```
RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN=<provisionado>
RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN=<provisionado>
```

**Decisão de storage — mover para o `.env` raiz LINKED_ENV.** Padrão do projeto (auditado): o `.env` raiz `/v2/.env.concertacaoamazonia.com.br.sa` é onde ficam secrets multi-ambiente com sufixo `_DEV/_HML/_PROD` (modelo: `SMTP_PASSWORD_*`, `DB_PASS_*`, `REDIS_PASSWORD_*`). O `.env` do site só tem secrets exclusivamente locais (`MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `OPCACHE_INVALIDATE_TOKEN`).

Como os tokens RD Station são **os mesmos em dev/hml/prod** (mesma conta RD da Concertação), mas precisam estar disponíveis nos 3 ambientes para o `wp-config.php` definir as constantes corretas no deploy phase3, **mover para o raiz** segue a convenção e habilita deploy automático:

| Variável (raiz LINKED_ENV) | Tipo RD | Notas |
|---|---|---|
| `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN_DEV` | API Key server-side | mesmo valor da prod (conta única) |
| `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN_HML` | API Key server-side | mesmo valor |
| `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN_PROD` | API Key server-side | mesmo valor |
| `RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN_DEV` | UUID de tracking client-side | reservado (tracker JS futuro) |
| `RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN_HML` | UUID de tracking client-side | reservado |
| `RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN_PROD` | UUID de tracking client-side | reservado |

> Alternativa considerada: **uma única var não-sufixada** (`RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN`) sem `_DEV/_HML/_PROD`. Funcionaria porque os 3 valores são idênticos, mas quebra convenção e impede uso futuro de chave de teste em dev. Trade-off pequeno mas escolho seguir o padrão.

Operações concretas:

1. Mover as 2 linhas de `docker-dev/sites/concertacao/.env` para `/Users/dcambria/scripts/server-tools/v2/.env.concertacaoamazonia.com.br.sa` com sufixo `_DEV`, `_HML`, `_PROD` (mesmo valor nas 3 — escrever via `env-writer-helper.sh`, único responsável por mexer em `.env`).
2. Remover as 2 linhas originais do `.env` do site.
3. O `wp-config.php` (gerado via bootstrap) já tem padrão de pegar do ambiente sufixado via `config-helper.sh`: `define( 'RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN', getenv( 'RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN_' . strtoupper( $env ) ) ?: '' );` — adicionar no template `wp-config.php` ou no helper de pós-bootstrap que injeta constantes (igual `SMTP_*`).
4. Verificar com `grep RDSTATION docker-dev/common/scripts/` se algum script já contempla; senão adicionar.

A constante PHP final lida pelo mu-plugin é `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN` (sem sufixo) — o helper resolve o sufixo `_DEV/_HML/_PROD` em build time.

| Aspecto | API Key (escolhido) | OAuth 2.0 (descartado) |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | 1 constante em `wp-config.php` (`RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN`) | App no AppStore + callback + dialog + token exchange + refresh |
| Storage | só `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN` em wp-config (via `.env`) | `client_id`/`client_secret` em wp-config + `refresh_token`/`access_token` em option encrypted |
| Renovação | nunca | a cada 23h (cron) |
| Endpoint | `POST /platform/conversions?api_key=X` | `POST /platform/events` com Bearer token |
| Limitação | só `event_type=CONVERSION` (suficiente p/ newsletter) | qualquer evento custom |
| Linhas de código | ~120 | ~400 |

### Endpoint usado

```http
POST https://api.rd.services/platform/conversions?api_key={RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "event_type": "CONVERSION",
  "event_family": "CDP",
  "payload": {
    "conversion_identifier": "newsletter-footer-concertacao",
    "email": "lead@example.com",
    "cf_uf": "PA",
    "tags": ["newsletter", "concertacao-amazonia", "footer-form"],
    "legal_bases": [
      { "category": "communications", "type": "consent", "status": "granted" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Sucesso: `HTTP 200`. Erro: `400` (payload malformado) / `401` (api_key inválida) / `429` (rate limit — 120 req/min, folgado pra newsletter).

### Custom fields RD — pré-requisito manual

`cf_*` **precisa ser pré-cadastrado** no painel RD ou via `POST /platform/contacts/fields` antes do primeiro submit (payload com cf desconhecido é ignorado silenciosamente).

Recomendação:

| api_identifier | name | data_type | presentation_type | conteúdo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cf_uf` | "UF" | STRING | TEXT_INPUT | sigla UF do Brasil (AC, AM, PA, etc.) |
| `cf_consent_source` | "Origem do Consentimento" | STRING | TEXT_INPUT | URL completa onde o consentimento foi dado |
| `cf_consent_timestamp` | "Timestamp do Consentimento" | STRING | TEXT_INPUT | ISO 8601 do momento do submit |

**Setup inicial**: documentar em `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-formulario-rodape-unificado-design.md` como tarefa one-shot manual (ou criar script `scripts/rdstation-bootstrap-fields.php` que faz POST nos 3 fields, idempotente — checa se já existe via GET antes).

### Arquitetura: Form Action customizada (não hook `new_record`)

Em vez de hook `elementor_pro/forms/new_record` (genérico, dispara pra todo form), criamos uma **Form Action** que o user escolhe na aba "Actions After Submit" do widget Form. Vantagens:

- Aparece como toggle no editor — só forms que tiverem "RD Station (BIT)" selecionado disparam.
- Controles próprios na aba (conversion_identifier, mapping de fields, tags) — sem código.
- Falha do RD **nunca** quebra o submit do form (graceful degradation): mesmo se a API retornar 4xx/5xx ou timeout, a Action retorna sem chamar `add_error_message`. Tudo vai para o log.

### Estrutura da Form Action

Classe `BIT\RDStation\Form_Action` estendendo `\ElementorPro\Modules\Forms\Classes\Action_Base`, registrada via:

```php
add_action('elementor_pro/forms/actions/register', function ($registrar) {
    $registrar->register(new \BIT\RDStation\Form_Action());
});
```

Métodos implementados:

| Método | O que faz |
|---|---|
| `get_name()` | retorna `'bit_rdstation'` (id interno) |
| `get_label()` | retorna `'RD Station (BIT)'` (label no painel) |
| `register_settings_section($widget)` | adiciona controles: `bit_rd_conversion_identifier` (text, default `newsletter-footer-concertacao`), `bit_rd_email_field` (select dos field IDs), `bit_rd_uf_field` (select dos field IDs), `bit_rd_tags` (text CSV), `bit_rd_consent_field` (select acceptance field opcional) |
| `run($record, $ajax_handler)` | monta payload, POST via `wp_remote_post` (timeout=8), trata resposta, loga sempre — **NÃO chama `add_error_message` em falha do RD** (graceful: submit do form não pode quebrar porque RD está fora do ar) |
| `on_export($element)` | retorna os controles para serem limpos no export do template |

### Storage de credenciais

Padrão BIT confirmado pelo agente 3 (lendo 45 mu-plugins do projeto): **toda credencial em `wp-config.php` como constante**. Zero settings page no admin. Modelo: `ses-mailer.php`.

Constantes em `wp-config.php` (multisite — colocar no escopo global, não por blog). As 2 primeiras vêm direto do `.env` via bootstrap; as 2 opcionais o operador define manualmente quando precisar:

```php
// vindas do .env via bootstrap (já provisionadas pelo user)
define( 'RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN', '...' );   // obrigatório — API Key server-side
define( 'RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN',  '...' );   // reservado (tracker JS futuro)

// opcionais — adicionadas manualmente quando necessário
define( 'BIT_RDSTATION_DEFAULT_TAGS', 'newsletter,concertacao' );   // tags injetadas em todo submit
define( 'BIT_RDSTATION_DEBUG',        false );                       // opt-in pra log verboso
```

Sem painel admin. Se faltar `RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN`, mu-plugin inicializa em "modo passivo" (Action ainda aparece no editor mas faz no-op + log warning a cada submit). O `RDSTATION_PUBLIC_TOKEN` não é lido por esta integração — fica esperando uso futuro.

### Logging

- Sempre loga 1 linha por submit (success / fail) em `wp-content/uploads/bit-rdstation-logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log` (gitignored — uploads não é versionado).
- `BIT_RDSTATION_DEBUG=true` → dump completo do payload + resposta.
- Rotação manual (se virar problema, expandir depois — YAGNI).

### LGPD — checkbox obrigatório no form

O form footer hoje **não tem checkbox de consentimento**. Para conformidade com LGPD ao enviar lead pro RD:

- Adicionar um `acceptance` field (Elementor Pro nativo) ao widget unificado, com texto pequeno tipo "Concordo em receber comunicações da Concertação Pela Amazônia."
- Field obrigatório no mobile e desktop (responsive — sempre visível).
- A Form Action lê esse field via `bit_rd_consent_field` setting; se não marcado, `legal_bases[].status="declined"` e ainda assim envia (RD cria o lead, mas não enviará marketing).
- Adicional: `cf_consent_source` = `home_url() + '/'`, `cf_consent_timestamp` = `wp_date('c')` (ISO 8601).

### Arquivos da Parte 2

- `wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-rdstation.php` (~250 linhas PHP)
- `docker-dev/common/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-rdstation.php` (cópia canônica)
- `scripts/rdstation-bootstrap-fields.php` (~80 linhas — one-shot idempotente pra criar cf_uf/cf_consent_*)

Sem JS, sem CSS (Action é só backend; os controles do painel são renderizados pelo Elementor).

### Pontos que precisam validação real (marcados [NÃO VERIFICADO] pelos agentes)

1. Schema exato de erro 400/422 — testar com curl payload inválido em conta real.
2. Comportamento com email em opt-out — testar com email descadastrado em conta sandbox.
3. Se `cf_consent_source` / `cf_consent_timestamp` chegam ao painel do RD como esperado.

Decisão: validar manualmente com curl + conta sandbox antes de wire-up no form de produção. Sem ambiente de teste oficial — RD oferece **conta Pro gratuita pra Integration Partner** (5k leads) que serve de sandbox.

### Roadmap futuro (fora desta entrega)

- Migrar pra OAuth se aparecer 2º site BIT integrando (multi-tenant justifica complexidade).
- Adicionar `/platform/events/batch` se acumular submits offline (PWA / form com retry queue).
- Webhook RD → WP pra capturar opt-outs (necessário se a Concertação fizer reativação por email transacional).

## Verificação end-to-end

### Parte 1 — Form responsivo

1. **Dev** (`cambrasmax.local:8484`): abrir o footer no editor Elementor, ativar Mobile no switcher device-aware, verificar que `form_name` mostra placeholder `_mobile` e que campos têm border-radius pill.
2. **Migration script**: rodar `--dry-run` primeiro, validar diff JSON, depois aplicar.
3. **Playwright gate** comparando screenshots desktop/tablet/mobile do footer antes vs depois.
4. **Submit funcional**: preencher email + região, verificar via `std wp db query "SELECT * FROM wp_e_submissions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3;"` que `form_regiao` recebeu o `value` da UF (ex: `AC`) e NÃO `"Região"`.
5. **Smoke /smoke**: gates 26 (WPML orphan) e 28 (stale paths Elementor) precisam continuar verdes. Gate de form (29 — `bypass_header=OK`) precisa funcionar.

### Parte 2 — RD Station

1. **Curl manual à API com API Key**: enviar payload mínimo (email + conversion_identifier) em conta sandbox antes de wire-up no form. Documentar resposta de sucesso e estrutura de erro 400 real (resolve um dos `[NÃO VERIFICADO]`).
2. **Bootstrap dos custom fields**: rodar `scripts/rdstation-bootstrap-fields.php` (`GET` para verificar existência, `POST` se não existir). Conferir no painel RD que `cf_uf`, `cf_consent_source` e `cf_consent_timestamp` aparecem nos campos do contato.
3. **Submit funcional**: preencher o form footer em dev com `BIT_RDSTATION_DEBUG=true`, verificar log em `wp-content/uploads/bit-rdstation-logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log` (1 linha sucesso + dump completo do payload/resposta).
4. **Confirmação no painel RD**: o contato aparece em "Leads", com `cf_uf=PA`, tags aplicadas e conversão "newsletter-footer-concertacao" no histórico de eventos do lead.
5. **Teste de falha graceful**: comentar `define( 'RDSTATION_PRIVATE_TOKEN', ... )` no `wp-config.php` temporariamente, submeter form — o submit do form **precisa continuar funcionando** (resposta 200 no admin-ajax, mensagem de sucesso visível) e o log precisa ter 1 linha de warning. Form **não pode quebrar** quando RD falha.
6. **LGPD**: confirmar via curl manual que `legal_bases[].status="granted"` chega como esperado e que o lead aparece como opt-in no painel RD.

'use strict';

const { test, expect } = require('@playwright/test');
const path = require('path');
const fs = require('fs');

try { require('dotenv').config({ path: path.join(__dirname, '..', '.env.local') }); } catch {}

const screenshotsDir = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'screenshots', 'contact-form');

test.beforeAll(() => {
  fs.mkdirSync(screenshotsDir, { recursive: true });
});

test('formulário de contato: fill + submit', async ({ page }) => {
  if (process.env.SKIP_CONTACT_FORM === 'true') {
    test.skip(true, 'SKIP_CONTACT_FORM=true — envio ignorado para evitar spam em produção');
    return;
  }

  await page.goto('/contato/', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);

  // Screenshot antes do preenchimento

  const messageSelector = 'textarea';

form.dataset.bitFormNameMobile;\n        var headingTarget = form.querySelector('.elementor-form-heading, .elementor-field-group-html h2, .elementor-field-group-html h3, .elementor-field-group-html h4');\n        if (headingTarget) {\n            if (!headingTarget.dataset.bitFormNameDesktop) {\n                headingTarget.dataset.bitFormNameDesktop = headingTarget.textContent;\n            }\n            if (device === 'mobile' && nameMobile) {\n                headingTarget.textContent = nameMobile;\n            } else if (device === 'tablet' && nameTablet) {\n                headingTarget.textContent = nameTablet;\n            } else {\n                headingTarget.textContent = headingTarget.dataset.bitFormNameDesktop;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    function initAll() {\n        document.querySelectorAll('.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive').forEach(applyResponsiveText);\n    }\n\n    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {\n        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initAll);\n    } else {\n        initAll();\n    }\n\n    // Re-aplica em resize / orientation change\n    var resizeTimer;\n    window.addEventListener('resize', function () {\n        clearTimeout(resizeTimer);\n        resizeTimer = setTimeout(initAll, 120);\n    });\n    window.addEventListener('orientationchange', initAll);\n})();\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Adicionar enqueue do JS no mu-plugin**\n\nEm `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php`, **dentro do `wp_enqueue_scripts` callback** (junto com o # Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns

    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
```

**API deviation — `remove_control` + `add_responsive_control` instead of `update_control` for `form_name`:**
- Plan assumed `update_control('form_name', ['responsive' => true])` would work
- Implementer discovered (correctly) that Elementor requires explicit sibling controls (`form_name_tablet`, `form_name_mobile`) to be _created_ in the PHP control stack — `update_control` alone on the base control does not generate the siblings
- The solution (`remove_control` + `add_responsive_control`) follows Elementor's documented responsive control pattern exactly, as confirmed by reading Elementor Core's `add_responsive_control()` source

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    {DESCRIPTION}

    ## Requirements / Plan

    {PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** {BASE_SHA}
    **Head:** {HEAD_SHA}

    ```bash
    git diff --stat {BASE_SHA}..{HEAD_SHA}
    git diff {BASE_SHA}..{HEAD_SHA}
    ```

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
```

---

## Code Review: `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` (Tasks 1 + 2)

**Git range:** `8d2843a292..450258a72c` — 237 lines added, 1 file.

---

### Strengths

**Correct diagnosis of plan defect (line 88, critical):** The plan proposed `update_control('form_name', ['responsive' => true])` — that API does not exist in Elementor. The implementer correctly identified this, read the Elementor source, and pivoted to `remove_control() + add_responsive_control()`. This is precisely the right approach and shows the implementer audited the plan's assumptions before committing.

**Guard improvement over plan (line 28):** The plan's guard was `! did_action('elementor_pro/init') && ! class_exists(...)`. That is factually a bug in the plan — `elementor_pro/init` fires on the `init` hook, which runs *after* `plugins_loaded`. At priority 20 of `plugins_loaded`, `did_action('elementor_pro/init')` always returns `0`, making the AND guard always false-of-the-first-operand and relying entirely on the `class_exists` half anyway. The implementation correctly drops `did_action` and uses only `class_exists('\ElementorPro\Plugin')` — this is a bug fix, not a simplification.

**Idempotence guards are sound (lines 82–84, 122–124, 127, 172):** Two-tier guarding: a fast-path outer guard that skips the expensive `update_control` call when both controls are already present, plus independent inner guards for each block. Trace through partial-state (only one of the two controls present from a hypothetical half-run): each inner block correctly handles it. No state corruption possible.

**Doc comment on `_register_form_control_hooks` (lines 36–53):** This is a model for WHY-not-WHAT comments. It explains the duplication mode, the empirical validation context, and the structural difference between top-level controls and repeater sub-controls. Reviewers can reproduce the reasoning without reading Elementor source.

**Namespace usage is correct (line 15 before line 17):** `namespace` declaration precedes `defined()`, PHP requires this. `const VERSION` and `const WIDGET_CLASS` are correctly scoped and accessible inside the closures because PHP closures inherit the file-level namespace.

**No premature CSS/JS (verified):** The file contains zero `wp_enqueue_*`, `wp_register_*`, `add_filter('elementor/widget/render_content')`, or any render-time code. Tasks 3–5 are correctly deferred. `WIDGET_CLASS` is forward-declared as a constant for use by Task 3 — that is the right architectural choice (avoids hardcoding the string in multiple future places).

**File-structure rule respected:** Only the `.php` exists. `.css` and `.js` are not created yet. The plan defines them for Tasks 4–5 — no jumping ahead.

**Backward compatibility confirmed (verified against Elementor Pro source):** Control registration only mutates the widget's class-level control schema at runtime. Saved `_elementor_data` post_meta for existing forms (like footer 72234) is untouched. `get_settings_for_display()` cascades missing `_tablet`/`_mobile` keys gracefully to the base value. Existing forms will not regress visually or functionally before Task 7's migration script runs.

**Multisite-safe:** `Network: true` header is present. The plugin registers no per-blog state, no `switch_to_blog`, no per-site options.

---

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

**None.** There are no data-loss risks, security issues, or broken functionality in Tasks 1 + 2.

The `field_options_empty` control being added to the editor schema without a corresponding render path is *by design* (Task 3 is pending). If someone saves a value into `field_options_empty` before Task 3 is deployed, nothing breaks — Elementor just stores the value in `_elementor_data` and ignores it at render time. This is safe.

---

#### Important (Should Fix Before Task 3)

**[1] Hook priorities 10 and 11 have no documented rationale** — `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` lines 59 and 66.

The two hooks operate on independent controls (`form_name` vs `form_fields` repeater), so they are not order-dependent on each other. Priority 10 and 11 are chosen to run after Elementor's own control registration (which fires at default priority on the same action), but there is no comment explaining this. If another plugin or future BIT mu-plugin hooks onto `elementor/element/form/section_form_fields/before_section_end` at priority 9 and modifies `form_name` or `form_fields`, the reasoning for this staggered ordering would need to be revisited.

Fix: add a one-line comment above each `add_action` call:

```php
// Priority 10/11 — runs after Elementor Pro's own control registration (fires at default=10).
// Two separate priorities to keep each callback atomic and independently removable.
```

**[2] `_make_repeater_fields_responsive` silently passes when `placeholder` doesn't exist in `$fields`** — line 127.

The inner guard is `! isset($fields['placeholder_tablet']) && isset($fields['placeholder'])`. If Elementor Pro changes the internal control key for placeholder (unlikely but possible across major Elementor Pro versions), the placeholder block is silently skipped with no log. The `field_options_empty` block runs regardless (it has no dependency on `placeholder` existing), which is correct. But the function still calls `update_control('form_fields', ...)` at line 232 even if both inner blocks were skipped due to guards — meaning a no-op database write to the control schema. Low-impact but worth noting.

Fix: add an early-return before `update_control` if no changes were actually made:

```php
$changed = false;
// ... inside each if block: $changed = true;
if ( ! $changed ) {
    return;
}
$element->update_control( ... );
```

**[3] `field_options_empty` positioning in the editor panel is undefined** — lines 183–228.

`field_options` (Elementor Pro native, TEXTAREA) appears right after `placeholder` in the repeater tab. The new `field_options_empty` controls are appended to the end of the `$fields` array via array assignment. In PHP associative arrays, newly added keys go to the end. Elementor renders repeater fields in array key order, so `field_options_empty` will appear at the bottom of the repeater panel — below `select_size`, `allow_multiple`, and other controls — rather than logically adjacent to `field_options`. This is a UX issue, not a correctness bug, but it affects the editor experience for Task 5's manual validation step.

There's no clean Elementor API to insert a field at a specific position in a repeater's `$fields` array. A workaround is to rebuild the array in insertion order before calling `update_control`. This should be done in Task 2 before editor testing begins.

---

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**[4] The `defined('ABSPATH') || exit` comes after `const VERSION` and `const WIDGET_CLASS`** — well, actually: `namespace` is at line 15, `defined()` is at line 17, `const VERSION` is at line 19. The guard at line 17 protects lines 19+. This is correct. But if a PHP file scanner (phpcs, linter) ever triggers on "namespace before guard", it's worth noting the ordering is intentional. A comment `// Must follow namespace declaration; guard against direct file access` would close the loop.

**[5] The `$args` parameter in `_make_form_name_responsive` and `_make_repeater_fields_responsive` is unused** — lines 78 and 113. PHP will not warn (no `declare(strict_types=1)`) but phpcs/psalm would flag it. Rename to `$_args` to signal intentional non-use.

**[6] Line count (237 vs plan's ~150):** The additional ~87 lines are entirely accounted for by the explicit `_tablet` and `_mobile` sibling fields that the plan assumed Elementor would auto-generate from `responsive => true`. Since Elementor does not auto-generate them for repeater sub-controls, the explicit definitions are necessary. This is not accidental bloat — it is the correct minimum to make the editor controls work. The line count is justified.

---

### Recommendations

**Before Task 3 starts:** Address issue [3] (field position in repeater panel). Once Task 3's filter and Task 5's JS are in, the editor will be validated manually (plan Task 3 Step 3) — if `field_options_empty` appears at the bottom of a long panel, it may be missed during validation. A few lines to rebuild the `$fields` array in insertion order (around `field_options`) would make Task 5's manual validation reliable.

**Task 3 filter design note (for the implementer):** When Task 3's `elementor/widget/render_content` filter adds the `data-bit-placeholder-tablet/mobile` attrs, it will need to handle `select` elements differently — the `<select id="form-field-{id}">` tag does not have a `placeholder` attribute, so the filter should also inject `data-bit-field-options-empty-tablet/mobile` attributes for the JS to use when swapping the `<option disabled selected>` text. The existing plan's Task 3 code already does this via `field_options_empty_tablet`/`_mobile` keys from `get_settings_for_display()`. Confirm those keys will be populated correctly by Elementor's responsive cascade from the controls registered in Task 2 before proceeding.

---

### Assessment

**Ready for next task? Yes.**

Tasks 1 and 2 are architecturally sound. The Elementor control registration is correct, idempotent, backward-compatible, and doesn't touch CSS/JS prematurely. The one issue worth addressing before Task 3 is [3] (repeater field ordering for editor UX), but it does not block Task 3's implementation — it only affects the manual editor validation step. Issues [1] and [2] are documentation and defensive-coding improvements that can be applied in a single cleanup commit before or alongside Task 3.

**Status: DONE**

## Report

### Sync strategy

- **Sync IN:** `rsync -a` from worktree to main repo before editing.
- **Sync OUT:** Same `rsync -a` after each edit, before running container commands.
- **Revert:** The file was NOT tracked in main HEAD (`git ls-files --error-unmatch` returned error). Revert was `rm` of the file from main. Confirmed removed.

### Key finding during implementation

The plan's code was incorrect about the class injection strategy. `elementor/widget/render_content` receives only the **inner** HTML of the widget (the `<form>` and its children), NOT the outer `<div class="elementor-widget-form">`. That outer wrapper is emitted by `before_render()` via `_wrapper` render attributes.

The implementation was split into two hooks:
1. **`elementor/frontend/widget/before_render` (action):** calls `$widget->add_render_attribute('_wrapper', 'class', WIDGET_CLASS)` and injects `data-bit-form-name-tablet/mobile` on the outer wrapper div.
2. **`elementor/widget/render_content` (filter):** injects `data-bit-placeholder-tablet/mobile` on `<input>/<textarea>` and `data-bit-placeholder-*` + `data-bit-field-options-empty-tablet/mobile` on `<select>`, matched by `id="form-field-{custom_id}"` with `preg_replace(..., 1)`.

### Code added

`/Users/dcambria/scripts/server-tools/v2/docker-dev/sites/concertacao/.claude/worktrees/feat-footer-form-unified-part1/wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` — lines 270–396: `_register_render_filter()` function, called from the `plugins_loaded` callback.

### Validation results

- `php -l`: `No syntax errors detected`
- `elementor flush-css`: `Success: Flushed the Elementor CSS Cache`
- PHP-FPM reload: exit 0
- `grep -oE 'class="[^"]*elementor-widget-form[^"]*"'`: **2 matches**, both containing `bit-form-responsive` at the start of the class string:
  - `class="bit-form-responsive elementor-element elementor-element-18af5b7 ... elementor-widget-form"`
  - `class="bit-form-responsive elementor-element elementor-element-e85e505 ... elementor-widget-form"`
- `grep data-bit-*`: no `data-bit-placeholder-*` or `data-bit-form-name-*` yet (expected — no tablet/mobile values set in editor yet). The `data-bit-fx-*` present are from an unrelated plugin.
- `has_filter("elementor/widget/render_content")`: `bool(true)` — render_content filter confirmed registered.

### Commit hash

`917640d121` — `feat(form-responsive): filter de render injeta classe escopo + data-attrs responsivos`

### Self-review findings

- **Idempotência da classe:** `add_render_attribute('_wrapper', 'class', ...)` é o método nativo do Elementor — ele garante que a classe é adicionada ao array de classes do wrapper, sem duplicação, mesmo se chamado duas vezes.
- **Limit=1 nos regexes de input/select:** confirmado — todos os `preg_replace` passam `1` como quarto argumento.
- **Seletor `id="form-field-{custom_id}"`:** correto — confirmado no HTML real (linha 2929 do dump: `id="form-field-form_email_desk"`). O `preg_quote` no `$escaped_id` protege contra IDs com caracteres especiais.
- **Atributos vazios:** todos os injects têm guarda `if ( $ph_tablet !== '' )` antes de montar o atributo — atributos vazios nunca são emitidos.
- **Select recebe `$ph_attrs + $foe_attrs`:** o `$select_extra` combina ambos, portanto o select recebe todos os 4 possíveis atributos de uma vez, em um único `preg_replace`.
- **Regressão:** nenhum — o hook `before_render` retorna imediatamente para widgets que não são `form`, e o filter `render_content` também retorna `$content` intacto para não-form widgets.

---

## Code Review — Task 3: `bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` (129 lines added, commit `917640d121`)

---

### Plan Deviation Assessment

The plan's Task 3 code attempted to inject the `bit-form-responsive` class via `preg_replace` on `render_content`, targeting `class="[^"]*elementor-widget-form[^"]*"`. This would silently fail because `elementor/widget/render_content` receives only the inner HTML of the widget container — the outer `<div class="elementor-widget-form ...">` wrapper is emitted before the filter runs.

The implementer diagnosed this correctly and split into two hooks:
- `elementor/frontend/widget/before_render` (action) — has access to the `$widget` object before the wrapper div is emitted, allowing `add_render_attribute('_wrapper', ...)` to mutate it.
- `elementor/widget/render_content` (filter) — operates on inner HTML where `<input>`, `<textarea>`, and `<select>` elements live.

This deviation is architecturally sound. The plan's code would have been a no-op.

---

### Strengths

**Line 287–316 — `_register_render_filter()` docblock:** The comment explicitly explains why two hooks are needed instead of one. This is exactly the kind of non-obvious "why" comment that future maintainers need. Well placed.

**Lines 296, 302 — Early exit in `before_render`:** `if ($widget->get_name() !== 'form')` fires before any work. Cost for non-form widgets is a single string comparison.

**Lines 322–325 — Early exit in `render_content`:** Same pattern. Non-form widgets exit in one comparison. Critical for a filter that runs on every widget render across the whole page.

**Lines 329–331 — Empty fields guard:** `if (empty($settings['form_fields']) || !is_array(...))` catches degenerate cases (form with no fields) and type-unsafe data cleanly.

**Lines 339, 346–350, 354–360 — `preg_quote` + `esc_attr`:** `preg_quote($field_id, '/')` prevents regex injection from user-controlled `custom_id` values. `esc_attr()` on every injected attribute value. Security posture is correct.

**Lines 365–367 — Skip when nothing to inject:** `if ($ph_attrs === '' && $foe_attrs === '') { continue; }` prevents the regex from running at all when no responsive values were set. The `render_content` filter is a pure no-op for forms that don't use responsive settings. Other site forms (contact form, cultura newsletter) are unaffected by the filter.

**Lines 371–376 — Regex for input/textarea:** Pattern `(<(?:input|textarea)[^>]*\bid="form-field-{id}"[^>]*?)(\/?>)` was tested against all significant permutations:
- id attribute in any position (first, last, middle) — matches correctly in all cases
- self-closing `/>` — captured in `$2`, injection lands before it
- `<select>` — excluded by the `(?:input|textarea)` alternation, correctly handled by the separate select pattern
- Elementor's real rendered output (`size=`, `required=`, `aria-required=`, `placeholder=` in any order) — confirmed match

**Lines 381–387 — Regex for select:** `(<select[^>]*?\bid="form-field-{id}"[^>]*?)(>)` — `<select>` has no `type=` attribute, and the regex correctly does not require one. Tested and confirmed matching.

**Lines 340–360 — `trim()` on all values:** Whitespace-only entries (a user typing a space in a field) produce `''` after trim and are correctly skipped. No phantom empty attributes emitted.

---

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix Before Task 4)

**`before_render` adds `WIDGET_CLASS` unconditionally to ALL form widgets** (`bit-elementor-form-responsive.php`, lines 301–302)

```php
// Current — unconditional:
$widget->add_render_attribute( '_wrapper', 'class', $widget_class );
```

Every Elementor Form widget on the entire site gets `bit-form-responsive` added to its wrapper, regardless of whether it has any responsive settings. This is currently harmless in isolation (Task 3 adds no CSS yet), but Task 4 (the CSS) is directly gated on this class and contains opinionated visual rules:

```css
/* From Task 4 plan */
.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive .elementor-field-textual {
    background: transparent;
    border: 2px solid #fff;
    color: #fff;
}
```

This CSS will apply to the contact form and the `/cultura/` newsletter form the moment Task 4 lands, because they will already carry the class from Task 3. The plan's assumption ("CSS escopado em `.bit-form-responsive` evita afetar outros forms") is only valid if the class is not universally added — which is exactly what the current implementation does.

Fix: make the class injection conditional on the form having any tablet/mobile settings populated:

```php
$name_tablet = trim( $settings['form_name_tablet'] ?? '' );
$name_mobile = trim( $settings['form_name_mobile'] ?? '' );

// Check if any field has responsive settings
$has_responsive = $name_tablet !== '' || $name_mobile !== '';
if ( ! $has_responsive ) {
    foreach ( $settings['form_fields'] ?? [] as $f ) {
        if ( trim( $f['placeholder_tablet'] ?? '' ) !== ''
            || trim( $f['placeholder_mobile'] ?? '' ) !== ''
            || trim( $f['field_options_empty_tablet'] ?? '' ) !== ''
            || trim( $f['field_options_empty_mobile'] ?? '' ) !== '' ) {
            $has_responsive = true;
            break;
        }
    }
}

if ( $has_responsive ) {
    $widget->add_render_attribute( '_wrapper', 'class', $widget_class );
}
```

This should be resolved before Task 4 creates the CSS, not after.

---

#### Important (Should Fix)

**`custom_id` empty-string fallback silently drops the `_id` fallback** (`line 334`)

```php
$field_id = $field['custom_id'] ?? $field['_id'] ?? '';
```

`??` only substitutes when the left side is `null` or the key is absent. When Elementor stores `custom_id` as `''` (empty string — the default when the user leaves the field blank), `??` returns `''` and the `_id` fallback is never reached. The subsequent `if (!$field_id) continue` then skips the field entirely.

In the current footer form this is latent — both fields (`form_email`, `form_regiao`) have explicit `custom_id` set. But the mu-plugin will ship to `common/mu-plugins/` and be usable on other projects and future forms. Any form field without a `custom_id` set would silently not receive its responsive attributes.

Fix:
```php
$field_id = ( $field['custom_id'] ?? '' ) ?: ( $field['_id'] ?? '' );
```

`?:` (Elvis) substitutes on falsy, which correctly catches both absent keys and empty strings.

---

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**Double-space artifact in self-closing input tags** (`line 372, pattern + injection`)

Elementor renders inputs as `<input ... placeholder="E-mail" />` (trailing space before `/>` is common in its output). The lazy `[^>]*?` captures that trailing space into `$1`. Since `$ph_attrs` starts with a space (`' data-bit-...'`), the result is `placeholder="E-mail"  data-bit-.../>` (two spaces). This is valid HTML and browsers parse it correctly, but it's cosmetically inconsistent.

Not worth a regex rewrite — it's genuinely harmless. Flag it as known behavior or add `rtrim($1)` in the replacement if code cleanliness matters.

**`$foe_attrs` abbreviation** (`lines 354–362`)

`$foe_tablet` / `$foe_mobile` / `$foe_attrs` — "foe" requires reading the comment to decode as "field_options_empty". The comment directly above (`--- field_options_empty_tablet / _mobile (select only) ---`) makes it readable in context, but a slightly longer abbreviation (`$foe_empty_tablet` or `$empty_opt_tablet`) would be self-documenting. Not a blocking concern given the nearby comment.

**`add_render_attribute` does not deduplicate class values in Elementor**

The code comment on line 301 says "add_render_attribute é idempotente internamente" which is partially true: subsequent calls on the same element key return the existing value without error. However, calling `add_render_attribute('_wrapper', 'class', 'bit-form-responsive')` twice would emit `class="... bit-form-responsive bit-form-responsive"`. Since `before_render` fires once per render per widget, this is not a real risk in the current architecture — but the comment overstates the guarantee. Adjust the comment to "fires once per render; no dedup mechanism in Elementor."

---

### Assessment

**Ready for next task?** No — with a conditional fix first.

**Reasoning:** The class injection unconditionally targets all Form widgets sitewide. Task 4 (the CSS with `border: 2px solid #fff; color: #fff;`) will break the contact form and the cultura newsletter form the moment it's applied. The `custom_id` fallback bug is latent but should be fixed while the code is fresh. Both are two-line fixes and should be done before Task 4 is implemented.

I now have all the information needed for a complete, authoritative review. Here is my assessment:

---

## Senior Code Review — Task 4 (CSS + Enqueue)

**Files reviewed:**
- `/wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.css` (127 lines, new file)
- `/wordpress/wp-content/mu-plugins/bit-elementor-form-responsive.php` (diff: 25 lines added)

---

### Strengths

**CSS scope discipline is exemplary.** Every single rule — desktop and mobile — is prefixed with `.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive`. There is zero risk of leaking styles to other forms on the site. This is exactly right.

**Delta coverage is complete.** The 6 mobile deltas required by the spec (#3–#8) are all present and correctly separated between a base desktop block and a `@media (max-width: 767px)` block. The tablet comment is honest ("herda desktop — sem bloco separado").

**Enqueue architecture is correct.** `wp_register_style` runs in `wp_enqueue_scripts`; `wp_enqueue_style` fires inside `before_render`. The comment on line 317–321 correctly explains that WP deduplicates via `$wp_styles->done`. The docblock at line 288–289 correctly states the conditional load rationale.

**The FOUC risk is handled.** `before_render` fires during Elementor's render loop, which happens after `wp_head` has already printed. However, Elementor's built-in mechanism (`elementor/frontend/after_enqueue_scripts` + WordPress's `wp_print_late_styles` called inside `wp_footer`) ensures late-enqueued styles ARE printed in the footer `<style>` block or `<link>` tag. The CSS is ~600 bytes gzipped. For a footer form (below the fold), there is no FOUC — the form is not visible when the page first paints. This is an acceptable pattern for this specific placement.

**`!important` use is justified.** Lines 89–91: `width: 100% !important` and `max-width: 100% !important` on `.elementor-field-group` are needed to override Elementor's inline `width` style injected by the column-layout engine. `margin-bottom: 0 !important` overrides Elementor's field spacing that would otherwise double with the `gap: 14px` on the wrapper. All three are standard practice for this class of override.

**Color comments in the file header** correctly document where each value comes from (footer green, white, mint). The spec comment is preserved. Author and version header present.

---

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

**CSS.L37–43 + L95–102 — Hard-coded hex colors violate the project's mandatory CSS variable convention.**

The `wordpress/CLAUDE.md` states explicitly:

> "CSS: SEMPRE usar variáveis pareadas com Global Colors do Elementor. Nunca use valores hex diretamente — sempre use `var(--e-global-color-*)`."

The child theme `style.css` (lines 112–116) already defines the relevant form variables:
- `--form-botao: var(--e-global-color-1e2de0e)` — `#FFFFFF`
- `--form-border: var(--e-global-color-9e25231)` — `#FFFFFF`
- `--form-placeholder: var(--e-global-color-a910fcf)` — `#656568` (note: this is for generic forms; footer form placeholder is white/mint, no variable exists yet — see below)
- `--white: var(--e-global-color-f589ade)` — `#FFFFFF`
- `--black: var(--e-global-color-f7de0e8)` — `#000000`

The problem is that `#0d3a2c` (footer dark green) and `#7fb088` (mint) have **no corresponding CSS variable** in the theme at all — neither as a `--e-global-color-*` nor as a named custom property. They should, but they don't exist yet.

**Fix:** Two options, in order of correctness:

1. **Preferred:** Add the missing Global Colors in Elementor Kit (ID 2553), regenerate the CSS kit, add the variable aliases to `style.css`, then use `var(--footer-bg)` and `var(--footer-placeholder-mobile)` (or similar) in `bit-elementor-form-responsive.css`.

2. **Acceptable short-term (before the Global Colors are added):** Add the CSS custom properties directly in `bit-elementor-form-responsive.css` as a `:root` block at the top of the file, with a clear comment marking them as "pending Elementor Global Color registration":

```css
/* Pending: register these in Elementor Global Colors (Kit 2553) */
:root {
    --footer-bg-verde: #0d3a2c;        /* Footer dark green — fundo do rodapé */
    --footer-mint: #7fb088;            /* Mint green — placeholder mobile */
}
```

Then use `var(--footer-bg-verde)` and `var(--footer-mint)` throughout the file. This creates a single source of truth inside the file and documents the gap. It does not fully satisfy the `CLAUDE.md` rule but it's better than naked hex everywhere.

The occurrences to fix: CSS lines 42, 98, 106 (`#0d3a2c`), lines 107, 112 (`rgba(127, 176, 136, 0.85)` — derived from `#7fb088`).

The `#fff` and `border: 2px solid #fff` references can be replaced with `var(--white)` and `var(--form-border)` immediately, since those variables exist.

---

#### Important (Should Fix)

**CSS.L51–53 — `select option[disabled]` color rule has zero cross-browser effect and creates dead code.**

```css
.elementor-widget-form.bit-form-responsive select.elementor-field option[disabled] {
    color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.65);
}
```

Styling individual `<option>` elements via CSS is not supported in Chromium/Chrome or Firefox on any OS — browsers ignore color, background, and font rules on `<option>` elements because the dropdown is rendered by the OS/native control. On macOS and Windows, the OS native select popup is used and CSS styles on `<option>` are stripped. On Firefox for some Linux distros, this may work.

**The rule on lines 51–53 and lines 109–112 is dead code on the two browsers used by >99% of Concertação's audience.** The option text color in the dropdown will always be the system default, not the specified value.

This is not harmful (browsers ignore it silently), but it adds confusion because it makes a reviewer think this is doing something when it is not. The actual styling of the "empty option" text in the closed select (the selected/visible state) is done via `color` on the `select` element itself when `option[disabled][selected]` has no value — which IS inherited. So the desired effect (dark green text on white background for the selected disabled option in mobile) is actually achieved by the `color: #0d3a2c` on the `select.elementor-field` rule in mobile (lines 95–102), not by the `option` rule.

**Fix:** Remove the two `option[disabled]` blocks (lines 51–53 and lines 109–112). They do nothing. Add a brief comment explaining that select option color in the closed state is inherited from the `select` element rule.

**CSS.L56–59 — Desktop `.elementor-field-type-submit` rule (`display: flex; align-items: center`) may conflict with Elementor's own layout.**

The desktop submit field is already laid out by Elementor's flex row (`elementor-form-fields-wrapper` is `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap`). Setting `display: flex` on the submit field-group and `align-items: center` without a complementary `justify-content` is a minor layout assumption. `align-items: center` vertically centers the button — good for alignment. `display: flex` on the field group forces the button element inside to grow. This is generally fine but it assumes no other flex children are in `.elementor-field-type-submit` that could be disrupted.

In practice this is a common pattern, but it should be validated visually (Step 4 of Task 4). Not blocking.

**PHP.L296–303 — `wp_enqueue_scripts` runs on the frontend AND in admin. The `wp_register_style` registration will fire on every admin page, not just frontend.**

```php
add_action( 'wp_enqueue_scripts', function () {
    wp_register_style( 'bit-form-responsive', ... );
} );
```

`wp_enqueue_scripts` does NOT fire in the admin — it is a frontend-only hook. This is actually correct by WordPress convention. However, since the `_register_render_filter()` function itself is called from `plugins_loaded` which runs everywhere (admin, AJAX, REST), the `add_action( 'wp_enqueue_scripts', ... )` call is registered on every request but the action itself only fires on frontend. This is fine — no admin-side risk. The comment could be clearer about this: "only fires on frontend requests."

Not a bug, but worth noting for future readers.

---

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**CSS.L61–67 — Button mobile rule missing `border: none` reset.**

On mobile, the button inherits the desktop rule `border: 2px solid #fff` from lines 63–64. The plan's spec says mobile button has "fundo transparente borda branca" — actually consistent. So the border is intentional on mobile too. But the mobile block (lines 121–125) never explicitly re-states the border — it inherits from the desktop rule. This is correct by CSS cascade, but if someone reads the mobile block in isolation they don't see the border. A comment like `/* border herdado do bloco desktop: 2px solid #fff */` would help maintainability.

**CSS — Missing `box-sizing: border-box` on mobile pill inputs.**

When `padding: 12px 20px` is added to the input in mobile (line 101), the `border: none` removal on line 99 avoids the border-box issue. But if the border is ever re-enabled or a parent has `box-sizing: content-box` override, the 24px radius pill could shrink oddly. Since `Hello Elementor` includes a base reset with `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }`, this is already inherited. No fix needed, just noting it passes correctly.

**CSS — No `:focus` or `:focus-visible` style for the mobile pill inputs.**

When inputs have `border: none` in mobile and the browser renders the focus ring, it will use the default outline, which on most browsers is a blue outline with 2px offset. The child theme defines `--focus-outline-color: var(--e-global-color-3091f92)` (`#C02975`). The footer form with white pill inputs will show a browser-default focus ring. Not critical since the footer is on a dark background and the focus ring will still be visible, but ideally a `.elementor-field-textual:focus` rule scoped to mobile would use `outline: 2px solid var(--focus-outline-color)`. Leave for Task 9/10 polish phase.

**Ready for next task?** Yes, with one fix before moving to Task 5.

The two `option[disabled]` dead-code blocks should also be removed to avoid misleading future reviewers. Neither fix is complex enough to block Task 5 if done concurrently — but both must be done before Task 10 (PR).
